title: APAC edge capacity ops scrub — week of May 7, 2028
content:
Attendees: Asha Patel (owner), Miguel Ortega, Connor Li, Priya Shah, Lena Voss, on-call: infra-weekend

Purpose: quick scrub to validate APAC edge priming ahead of the expected marketing-driven surge (mobile chat product) targeting SEA on May 12–15. Focus areas: available GPU headroom, prewarming schedule, heterogeneous instance mix, fallback routing, and runbook alignment for preemption risk.

Summary / tl;dr:
- Current committed edge pool for APAC (Tokyo, Singapore, Mumbai): 360 GPUs (equivalent v100-slices). Measured steady baseline utilization = 62% (7-day trailing avg). Planned short-term hedging target = 20% additional headroom (~72 GPUs) to absorb 48–72 hour surge.
- Short warmup experiment (n=3) improved median cold-start latency by 210ms for typical 512-token interactive traffic; cost ~2.8% extra token-cost during prewarm windows. Tradeoff: small cost vs SLO exposure.
- Identified one runbook drift: automated preemptible fallback policy was still set to fall back to a non-quantized variant (higher memory) — causes capacity pressure on certain hosts.
- Action items: immediate policy change to prefer quantized fallback variants, prioritize 40 GPU allocation from regional spare pool, and schedule a deeper priming dry run Wed 2028-05-10 02:00 UTC to validate cross-zone failover.

Observed metrics (as of 2028-05-09 06:00 UTC):
- Committed pool: 360 GPUs (raw) across 3 zones: TYO-1(140), SIN-1(120), BOM-1(100)
- Live instances: 338 GPUs (94% of committed online due to two maintenance hosts in BOM-1)
- 7d util avg: 62%
- 24h tail (p95 token latency, 512 tokens): 1540ms APAC edge aggregate
- Spike forecast probability (next 7 days): 28% (marketing campaign + partner launch)

Risk register items discussed:
1) Preemption cascade on heterogeneous hosts — root cause: some non-dedicated fleets still able to receive preemptible eviction signals; during last surge we saw chained migration delays causing 3–6min window of elevated latency. Mitigation: enforce eviction-migration isolation via taints for edge-prime nodes; scheduled change request INFRA-7382.
2) Runbook drift — older fallback policy (non-quantized) in control plane: causes memory oversubscription during fallback events. Short-term mitigation: override routing policy to tag model-variant=quantized for APAC edge; long-term: conformance test in CI for runtime variant compatibility.
3) Cross-zone priming gap — SIN-1 had only 40% of expected prefix cache hits due to differing traffic mix. Need to align prefix populations and prewarm sequences.

Decisions made:
- Approve temporary 20% capacity hedging for 72 hours starting 2028-05-11 00:00 UTC. Chargeback plan: Hosted-tier surge credit to product team; track cost vs SLO.
- Use quantized fallback variant as primary fallback for APAC edge until INFRA-7390 (runtime A/B) concludes.
- Nightly prewarm window 02:00–04:00 UTC for edge regions to reduce cold-start tail; initial trial for 48 hours only.

Planned ops & schedule:
- 2028-05-09 18:00 UTC: change routing policy to tag model-variant=quantized (Owner: Miguel Ortega, due: 2028-05-09 20:00 UTC)
- 2028-05-10 02:00 UTC: cross-zone dry run — simulate zone outage in SIN-1 and verify failover to TYO-1/BOM-1 (Owner: Connor Li, runbook owner Priya Shah)
- 2028-05-11 00:00 UTC: allocate 72 GPUs from spare pool to APAC edge, distributed TYO+SIN with one-zone limit to avoid single-point capacity drain (Owner: Lena Voss)
- 2028-05-11–2028-05-13: monitor surge; daily sync 08:30 UTC for first 72 hours (Owner: Asha Patel)

Notes on prewarm experiment (brief):
- Method: triggered a controlled prefix population job that stimulates typical user prompt shapes and pins kv-cache for top 25k prefixes. Ran 3 parallel jobs per zone for 30 minutes.
- Outcome: median p95 token latency improvement = -210ms; p99 improved by ~450ms; observed CPU overhead on host < 6% and estimated incremental cost = 2.8% of token spend for the window.
- Observations: warm cache improved small-chat interactions most; for large-batched inference there was negligible benefit. Implication: enable prewarm only for interactive-route tag.

Runbook & automation gaps called out:
- CI test missing: variant compatibility smoke test — should be gated on rollout pipeline (assigned INFRA-7390).
- Monitoring alert thresholds: p95 token latency alert for APAC edge currently at 2.0s — we will reduce to 1.6s for interactive routes during event windows. (Owner: Priya Shah)
- Eviction mitigation: need automated graceful rebalancer to pre-schedule container handoff 10 min before maintenance window (RFC in progress).

Action items (explicit):
- Miguel Ortega: update routing policy to prefer quantized fallback (done target 2028-05-09 20:00 UTC) — linked INFRA-7382
- Connor Li & Priya Shah: run cross-zone dry run 2028-05-10 02:00 UTC and capture latency + error profiles; publish notes to Confluence (due 2028-05-10 10:00 UTC)
- Lena Voss: request allocation 72 GPUs from spare pool and update capacity dashboard; ensure one-zone cap in allocation (due 2028-05-10 04:00 UTC)
- Asha Patel: lead daily surge sync 08:30 UTC 5/11–5/13 and consolidate incident channel plan into the operations binder (due 2028-05-11 07:30 UTC)
- Engineering-sre: add prewarm cost tag to billing pipeline so we can attribute extra spend to the marketing surge (Owner: SRE billing team, tracker: GH #4125)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we expand priming to include high-frequency prefixes for enterprise customers only? (pros: reduces latency for paying tiers; cons: added cost and cache fragmentation)
- What is the exact rollback threshold for the nightly prewarm window? Propose automated rollback if p95 increases by >10% vs baseline measured 24h prior.

Appendix: quick links and references
- INFRA-7382 (Jira): enforce taints & eviction isolation — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-7382
- Cross-zone dry-run playbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/APAC+Edge+Priming+Plan
- Dry-run runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal/pull/4125
- Slack thread: #gpu-ops: https://app.slack.com/client/TXXXXXXXX/C0123456789

Notes to self / scratch (informal):
- If SIN-1 traffic mix stays chatty while TYO uses more long-form, we should consider varying prefix population by zone rather than uniform.
- When surge subsides, evaluate whether we can refund or reassign spare GPUs to EU burst pool (cost ops).

Meeting end 2028-05-09 07:05 UTC.
